candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — assess emotional responses to illness, provide therapeutic support, and recognize psychosocial factors affecting health and self-management
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — diabetes distress and chronic-disease self-management burden
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize diabetes distress as a diabetes-specific emotional burden distinct from depressive or anxiety disorders and identify it as a clinically relevant concern that warrants routine assessment and support.

options.A: The client may be experiencing diabetes distress, an emotional burden specifically related to living with and managing diabetes that is distinct from depression or anxiety.
options.B: The statement establishes major depressive disorder because diabetes distress and depression are the same diagnosis.
options.C: Diabetes distress occurs only near the time of diagnosis and is unlikely after years of diabetes self-management.
options.D: The concern is not clinically relevant unless the client first develops a diabetes complication.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care define diabetes distress as emotional burdens and worries associated with living with and managing a demanding chronic condition. Diabetes distress is distinct from depression and anxiety, although they can coexist. The ongoing demands of medication dosing, glucose monitoring, food decisions, and physical activity can contribute to distress. ADA recommends screening for diabetes distress at least annually and repeating screening when treatment goals are not met, at transitional times, or when complications occur. B incorrectly equates distinct conditions. C is false because distress can occur throughout the diabetes course. D incorrectly minimizes a concern that should be acknowledged and addressed even without a complication.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Diabetes distress is a diabetes-specific emotional burden related to the ongoing demands of self-management, is distinct from depression/anxiety, can occur throughout the disease course, and should be routinely assessed and addressed.
candidate.source_document_title: Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.source_locator: Psychosocial Care — Diabetes Distress, Recommendation 5.45 and accompanying text: screen at least annually and at other critical times; diabetes distress refers to emotional burdens and worries associated with living with/managing diabetes, is distinct from depression and anxiety, and is associated with the constant behavioral demands of diabetes self-management
candidate.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
candidate.stem: A client with type 1 diabetes says, “I’m exhausted by the constant decisions about glucose, insulin, food, and activity, and I feel overwhelmed by diabetes every day.” The client does not describe persistent loss of interest or other symptoms sufficient to establish a depressive disorder. Which interpretation by the nurse is most appropriate?
